Requirement [2.5.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v25-credential-recovery)


| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE | [NIST §](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html) |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---:| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **2.5.3** | Verify password credential recovery does not reveal the current password in any way. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering)) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 640 | 5.1.1.2 |


If password is not stored in plain-text, it means hashing is used correctly like required by other requirement (2.4.1), then what 2.5.3 actually asks or how it can happen?

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE | [NIST §](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html) |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---:| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **2.4.1** | [MODIFIED] Verify that one of the following password hashing functions is used when storing passwords: argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt or PBKDF2. ([C6](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering)) | | ✓ | ✓ | 916 | 5.1.1.2 |

# Proposals

## v5.0
Delete current 2.5.3.

## v4.0.4

2.5.3 is level 1 and 2.4.1 is level 2, it would be breaking change (if do not consider it just an error). Can fix CWE to something more precise or just remove CWE.

comments.body:
Revealing of the current password also means that the app doesn't use secure way such as PSTN or time-based OTP in password recovery. I think it should be forbidden at level 1. Is my idea right that this is covered by other requirements such as [v5.0-2.2.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v22-general-authenticator-security)?

Note) I've posted this comment to be clear.

@elarlang do we state anywhere that passwords can only ever be stored in this way and can never be stored in any other way? Do we need to have a carve-out for passwords which need to be stored recoverably, e.g. for accessing 3rd party services? What do you think?

Your question opens actually another issue - make clear difference "user credential for application" and "external service authentication".

My proposal for removing 2.5.3 because it's covered by 2.4.1 is with clear "user credential for application" context.

For 3rd parties I think you don't start password recovery via some external application. Storing sensitive data is covered in V6.

> Your question opens actually another issue - make clear difference "user credential for application" and "external service authentication".

I raised this in #1277

title: 2.5.3 "do not send plain-text password on password recovery" is covered by password hashing
